decision: Validate the complete candidate-to-calibration-config bijection and Git SHA binding before starting any Qubes workload, then calibrate candidates sequentially.

reviews.reason: Length equality alone permits duplicate topology configs that omit a candidate; validation must prove a one-to-one mapping before evidence collection.
Invalid topology or SHA configuration must not partially execute synthetic workloads or produce partial evidence that could be mistaken for qualification data.

Parallel candidate calibration is faster wall-clock but contaminates RAM/CPU/probe-latency measurements through shared host contention. Sequential execution costs time but preserves measurement isolation and adds no runtime production surface.

alternatives.name: validate-each-config-lazily
alternatives.rejected: Can start one or more expensive Qubes workloads before discovering a duplicate, missing, unexpected, or wrong-SHA config.

alternatives.name: parallel-candidate-calibration
alternatives.rejected: Reduces wall-clock latency but creates cross-topology resource contention and weakens benchmark comparability.

alternatives.name: external-calibration-scheduler
alternatives.rejected: Adds infrastructure and lifecycle complexity without improving correctness for the bounded 1/2/3/4-worker candidate set.

qa: duplicate calibration topology IDs fail before runCalibration is called
unexpected topology IDs fail before runCalibration is called
wrong Git SHA fails before runCalibration is called
valid candidate calibrations execute with peak concurrency exactly one
mismatched returned provenance and no-winner evaluation remain fail-closed
lessons: A config-array length check is not a bijection proof.
Measurement throughput must not be optimized at the expense of resource-calibration isolation.
Preflight validation is highest value when it occurs before any distributed side effect, even synthetic ones.
